state.output: Here is a thorough analysis of the entire codebase. --- ## 1. Full Directory Tree (excluding `node_modules`) ``` /tmp/story_1b6f0b4967f2/ ├── .git/ # Git repository (not explored) ├── .instrument/ │ └── session.jsonl # Instrumentation session log ├── content/ # Empty — no content files at project root ├── dist/ # Compiled JavaScript output (tsc artifacts) │ ├── index.js │ ├── index.js.map │ ├── index.d.ts │ ├── index.d.ts.map │ ├── ssg.js │ ├── ssg.js.map │ ├── ssg.d.ts │ ├── ssg.d.ts.map │ ├── types.js │ ├── types.js.map │ ├── types.d.ts │ └── types.d.ts.map ├── node_modules/ # Installed dependencies ├── src/ # TypeScript source files │ ├── index.ts │ ├── ssg.ts │ └── types.ts ├── tests/ # Test files │ ├── ssg.test.ts │ └── content/ │ ├── getting-started.md │ └── hello-world.md ├── index.ts # Unrelated Express todo API (seed file, not part of SSG) ├── jest.config.js ├── package.json ├── package-lock.json └── tsconfig.json ``` **Key observation:** There is a stray `index.ts` at the project root that contains an **unrelated Express/Todo API**. The actual SSG entry point is `src/index.ts`. The root `index.ts` is likely a "seed" file from the scaffold and is **not** part of the static site generator. --- ## 2. All Source Files (the actual SSG code) ### `/tmp/story_1b6f0b4967f2/src/types.ts` — Type Definitions ```typescript export interface Frontmatter { title: string; date?: string; tags?: string[]; } export interface Page { frontmatter: Frontmatter; html: string; slug: string; } export interface SSGOptions { contentDir: string; outputDir: string; } ``` Three interfaces: - **`Frontmatter`** — represents parsed YAML frontmatter. `title` is required (falls back to slug if missing), `date` and `tags` are optional. - **`Page`** — the complete representation of a processed page: its frontmatter, HTML body, and slug. - **`SSGOptions`** — CLI input: paths to content directory and output directory. --- ### `/tmp/story_1b6f0b4967f2/src/ssg.ts` — Core SSG Logic This is the heart of the generator. It has six internal functions and one exported function: | Function | Lines | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `slugify()` | 7–10 | Converts a filename to a URL-safe slug (lowercased, spaces→hyphens, strips non-alphanum). | | `readMarkdownFiles()` | 12–19 | Reads a directory, filters for `.md` files, returns absolute paths. Returns `[]` if dir doesn't exist. | | `parsePage()` | 21–35 | Reads a `.md` file, parses frontmatter with `gray-matter`, converts Markdown to HTML with `marked`, builds a `Page` object. Falls back to slug as title if no `title` in frontmatter. | | `buildPageHTML()` | 37–67 | Wraps a `Page` in a full HTML5 document with inline template literals: ``, `<h1>`, optional date div, optional tags div, the body HTML, and a footer back-link. | | `buildIndexHTML()` | 69–95 | Generates `index.html` with a `<ul>` of links to all pages, each showing title, date, and tags. | | **`build()`** *(exported)* | 97–118 | Orchestrator: creates output dir if needed, reads markdown files, parses each, writes per-page `.html` files, then writes `index.html`. | **There is NO template system.** All HTML is generated via inline JavaScript template literals inside `buildPageHTML()` and `buildIndexHTML()`. There is no mechanism to load external template files, partials, or layouts. --- ### `/tmp/story_1b6f0b4967f2/src/index.ts` — CLI Entry Point Uses `yargs` to expose a single command: ``` ssg build --content ./content --output ./dist ``` Parses CLI args and calls `build()` from `ssg.ts`. Both `--content` and `--output` default to `./content` and `./dist` respectively. --- ## 3. Test Files ### `/tmp/story_1b6f0b4967f2/tests/ssg.test.ts` — 7 test cases | Test | What it checks | |---|---| | `generates index.html` | Verifies index.html exists and contains page titles, slugs, dates, tags from both test markdown files. | | `generates individual page HTML files` | Checks both `hello-world.html` and `getting-started.html` exist, have correct `<title>`, `<h1>`, markdown-rendered content, and back-link. | | `handles empty content directory` | Creates temp empty dir, verifies index.html is generated but has no `<li>` items. | | `handles non-existent content directory` | Passes a path that doesn't exist, verifies graceful fallback (empty index). | | `creates output directory if it does not exist` | Creates a new temp output dir, verifies it is created and populated. | | `index page lists all pages sorted` | Ensures both page titles appear in index (doesn't enforce order). | | `page without frontmatter uses slug as title` | Creates a markdown file with no YAML frontmatter, verifies the page title falls back to the filename slug. | Setup/teardown: `beforeEach` creates a fresh `/tmp/story_1b6f0b4967f2/tests/output/` directory; `afterEach` removes it. --- ### Test Content (Markdown fixtures) **`/tmp/story_1b6f0b4967f2/tests/content/hello-world.md`** ```markdown --- title: Hello World date: 2024-01-15 tags: - intro - typescript --- # Hello World This is a test page. ``` **`/tmp/story_1b6f0b4967f2/tests/content/getting-started.md`** ```markdown --- title: Getting Started date: 2024-02-20 tags: - guide --- # Getting Started Some **bold** and *italic* text. ## Installation Run `npm install` to get started. ``` --- ## 4. Frontmatter Parsing (detailed) In `src/ssg.ts`, line 22–26: ```typescript function parsePage(filePath: string): Page { const raw = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8'); const { data, content } = matter(raw); // gray-matter const html = marked.parse(content) as string; // marked const slug = slugify(path.basename(filePath)); return { frontmatter: { title: data.title || slug, // fallback to slug date: data.date, // optional tags: data.tags, // optional }, html, slug, }; } ``` The flow: 1. Read the raw `.md` file. 2. **`gray-matter`** parses YAML frontmatter between `---` delimiters, returning `{ data, content }`. 3. **`marked`** converts the remaining Markdown content to HTML. 4. A slug is derived from the filename. 5. If `data.title` is missing, the slug is used as the title. 6. `date` and `tags` are passed through as-is from YAML (no validation or transformation). 7. Returns a `Page` object. --- ## 5. How Pages Are Processed/Rendered (end-to-end) ``` CLI: ssg build --content ./content --output ./dist │ ▼ src/index.ts → build({ contentDir, outputDir }) │ ▼ src/ssg.ts build(): 1. fs.mkdirSync(outputDir, { recursive: true }) // ensure output dir exists 2. readMarkdownFiles(contentDir) // find *.md files 3. For each .md file: a. parsePage(file) // gray-matter + marked → Page object b. buildPageHTML(page) // inline template literal → full HTML string c. writeFileSync(outputDir/slug.html, html) 4. buildIndexHTML(pages) // inline template literal → index.html writeFileSync(outputDir/index.html, html) ``` **Rendering approach:** The HTML is generated by string interpolation inside template literals. There are no external template files, no template engine, no layout inheritance, no partials, no includes. The generator produces self-contained HTML5 pages with hardcoded structure. --- ## 6. `package.json` — Dependencies and Scripts **Scripts:** | Script | Command | |---|---| | `build` | `tsc` — compiles TypeScript in `src/` to `dist/` | | `test` | `jest --no-cache --verbose` | | `start` | `node dist/index.js` — runs the compiled CLI | **Runtime Dependencies:** | Package | Version | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `marked` | `^12.0.0` | Markdown-to-HTML conversion | | `gray-matter` | `^4.0.3` | YAML frontmatter parsing | | `yargs` | `^17.7.2` | CLI argument parsing | **Dev Dependencies:** | Package | Version | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `typescript` | `^5.3.3` | TypeScript compiler | | `jest` | `^29.7.0` | Test runner | | `ts-jest` | `^29.1.2` | Jest TypeScript transformer | | `@types/jest` | `^29.5.12` | Jest type definitions | | `@types/node` | `^20.11.0` | Node.js type definitions | | `@types/yargs` | `^17.0.32` | Yargs type definitions | --- ## 7. Template-Related Code **There is NO template system currently.** All HTML generation is done via inline template literals in two functions inside `src/ssg.ts`: - **`buildPageHTML()`** (lines 37–67) — Generates per-page HTML: ```typescript return `<!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head>...</head> <body> <main> <article> <h1>${title}</h1> ${dateHtml} ${tagsHtml} ${page.html} </article> </main> <footer> <a href="index.html">Back to index</a> </footer> </body> </html>`; ``` - **`buildIndexHTML()`** (lines 69–95) — Generates the index page: ```typescript return `<!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head>...</head> <body> <main> <h1>Pages</h1> <ul>${listItems}</ul> </main> </body> </html>`; ``` **Summary of template gaps:** - No external HTML/CSS template files exist anywhere in the project. - No layout/partial/inheritance mechanism. - No template engine (no EJS, Handlebars, Pug, etc.). - The HTML structure is hardcoded in template literals. - The `dist/` output confirms this — the compiled JS contains the same inline templates. --- ## Config Files **`/tmp/story_1b6f0b4967f2/jest.config.js`:** ```javascript module.exports = { preset: 'ts-jest', testEnvironment: 'node', roots: ['<rootDir>/tests'], testMatch: ['**/*.test.ts'], moduleFileExtensions: ['ts', 'js', 'json'], }; ``` **`/tmp/story_1b6f0b4967f2/tsconfig.json`:** ```json { "compilerOptions": { "target": "ES2020", "module": "commonjs", "lib": ["ES2020"], "outDir": "./dist", "rootDir": "./src", "strict": true, "esModuleInterop": true, "skipLibCheck": true, "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true, "resolveJsonModule": true, "declaration": true, "declarationMap": true, "sourceMap": true, "moduleResolution": "node" }, "include": ["src/**/*"], "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "tests"] } ``` --- That is the complete and thorough exploration of the codebase. Every source file, test, config, content fixture, and compiled artifact has been read and analyzed. </task_result> </task>
